data.title: Tropical Storm Edouard Impacts
data.description: The visitor center, trails, and waterways are open. Hikers and paddlers should be aware of fallen/leaning trees, washouts, debris, and damage to roads, trails, and bridges.

data.title: Site Closure – Adams Farm at Penn’s Hill
data.description: The Adams Farm at Penn’s Hill (John Adams and John Quincy Adams Birthplaces) is closed due to a major landscape treatment project. During construction, the entire site will be inaccessible. The Visitor Center and Peace field remain open and accessible.

data.title: Bag Policy
data.description: Bags larger than 9"x11"x5" are not permitted in the historic homes. The park does not have storage lockers for these items. Bags may not be left unattended and cannot be left with park staff. Anyone carrying a bag larger than 9"x11"x5" will not be admitted into the historic homes.

data.title: Tours Suspended Due To Emergency Phone System Outage
data.description: All tours Saturday, September 12th, have been suspended due to an emergency phone system outage. This outage has affected all phone lines inside the cave and inside the elevator system, preventing emergency calls to the surface should an incident occur. Once emergency phone service is restored, tours will resume with tickets available on a first-come-first-served basis at the visitor center. We appreciate your patience and understanding as we work to ensure the safety of our cave tours.

data.title: Crews Responding to Mount Tom Creek Fire
data.description: Fire managers are responding to a lightning fire in a remote area of Olympic National Park. The Mount Tom Creek Fire has burned 69 acres 5 miles west-northwest of Mount Olympus. Firefighters are using indirect confinement tactics as part of a full-suppression strategy. Backpackers are encouraged to consider alternative routes to the Hoh River Trail should fire activity increase. There are no evacuation orders or closures.

data.title: Scheduled Power Outage Monday, September 14th
data.description: The park will have a scheduled power outage from approximately 11:00 AM - 12:00 PM on Monday, September 14th. Thank you for your patience.

data.title: Park Reopened; Puʻuhonua Area and Section of Trail Remain Closed
data.description: Puʻuhonua o Honaunau National Historical Park has reopened following Hurricane Lowell. However, please note that the Puʻuhonua area of the park remains closed until further notice. Additionally, the 1871 Trail beyond Alahaka Ramp is also closed.

data.title: Empire Hill Climb: Saturday, September 19, 2026
data.description: The 2026 Empire Hill Climb will take place on Saturday, September 19, 2026. Drivers will race south on Wilco Rd from downtown Empire all the way to the Empire Bluff Trailhead area. Access to the Empire Bluff Trailhead will be limited. An alternative hike of similar terrain and distance is the Pyramid Point Trail to the overlook.

relatedRoadEvents.title: Empire Hill Climb on Wilco Road

data.title: Current East Rim Trail Status: Open
data.description: As of Thursday, September 10, 2026, the East Rim Trail System remains open. For more information, visit the website linked below. In good conditions the mountain bike trails are open 6 am-11 pm for bikers and as posted for other trail users. In wet or hazardous conditions, the trail will close to all users to prevent damage. Be flexible; conditions may change throughout the day.

data.title: INNER CANYON WATER SHUTOFFS
data.description: Beginning Sep. 6, no potable water will be available in the inner canyon, including along the Bright Angel Trail (1.5 Mile Resthouse, 3-Mile Resthouse, Havasupai Gardens day use and campground). All backpackers and hikers should carry water filtration and treatment OR carry all water with them.

data.title: WILDFIRE CLOSURES: Sunrise & northern trails. White River open.
data.description: Due to several active fires on the north side of the park, the following closures are in effect until further notice: Grand Park area & trails, Northern Loop Trail, Wonderland Trail from Carbon River Suspension Bridge to Frozen Lake, & associated backcountry campgrounds. White River Road & WR Campground reopened along with White River/Sunrise Trails. Sunrise Rd CLOSED to vehicles; open for pedestrians/bicycling only.

data.title: Elevator is Out-of-Service
data.description: The elevator at the Visitor Center is currently out-of-service, due to regularly scheduled maintenance. We apologize for the inconvenience and encourage visitors to visit the virtual tours available on our website.

data.title: North Beach and North Beach Road temporarily closed to visitors.
data.description: Point Reyes National Seashore has temporarily closed North Beach after a fishing vessel ran aground early on Friday, August 21st. To ensure public and responder safety during salvage operations, the closure area includes North Beach Road (aka Point Reyes Beach North), North Beach parking lot, 500 ft in all directions from the parking lot, and the area of beach in front of the parking lot.

data.title: Hilina Pali Road Shoulder Work Scheduled 9/14/26 to 11/19/26
data.description: Hilina Pali Road beyond the Maunaiki Trailhead will be closed to motorized vehicles on September 14, 2026 from 6 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday for shoulder work. Hikers, bicyclists and backcountry permit holders will be given access but should expect delays while heavy machinery works on the road. The entire road will be open to all use outside of those hours including weekends and holidays. The work is expected to be complete by November 19, 2026.

data.title: Parking and Road Closures in New Castle
data.description: Expect parking restrictions and road closures in Historic New Castle starting Wednesday, September 16 through Friday, September 18. Traffic delays are likely throughout the day. Please allow extra travel time and follow posted detours and parking instructions.

data.title: Haleakalā Visitor Center

data.title: Traffic advisory for the George Washington Patriot Run
data.description: On Sunday, September 13, from approximately 6 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. the Northbound and Southbound lanes on the GWMP between Mount Vernon Circle and West Boulevard will be closed to motor vehicle for the George Washington Patriot Run.

data.title: Ironman Triathlon: Sunday, September 20, 2026
data.description: Road closures on September 20, 2026. The race takes place on M-22 and will have a significant impact on local traffic. M-22 will be closed between Esch Road and Frankfort until 2 pm. Lake Michigan Road will not be accessible during the race. To avoid road closures, exit Lake Michigan Road by 8:30 am via Deadstream Road, Platte Road, or M-22 northbound. Anyone in the area of Lake Michigan Road after 8:30 am cannot depart until after 2 pm.

data.title: North Parking Lot at Osceola Landing to Close for Bridge Construction
data.description: The northernmost parking lot and co-located boat ramps at Osceola Landing will close week of 9/14 as part of the Hwy 243 Osceola Bridge replacement project. data.title: Preservation Work in Progress at The Oaks

Tours are limited to maximum of 5 visitors per reservation. Large groups and walk-in tours cannot be accommodated. To make a reservation, please call (334) 727-3200 or (334) 421-3246.

data.title: The Oaks Tours by Reservation Only
data.description: The Oaks, the historic home of Booker T. Washington is open by reservation only during an ongoing preservation and rehabilitation project. Built in 1899, the Queen Anne-style home is undergoing exterior rehabilitation work. Tours are limited to a maximum of 5 visitors per reservation. Large groups and walk-in tours will not be accommodated during this time. To make a reservation, please call (334) 727-3200 or (334) 421-3246.

data.title: Home of FDR - Partial Closure of Rose Garden
data.description: The planting beds, lawns, and paths of the Rose Garden will be under construction from late March 2026 lasting through fall of 2026. This rehabilitation will restore the crisp, level character of the garden, improve access and infrastructure, and re-install historic rose and peony varieties. During this period, the Burial Site viewing area should remain available, but occasional disruptions may restrict public access. The graves, marble monument, pet graves, and sundial will not be impacted by this project.

data.description: Due to unsafe bear‑human interactions, all of the Dryweed Island area's campsites, houseboat sites, and day use sites are closed. data.description: Bull elk are fast and unpredictable this time of year and can seriously injure people. If an elk charges, run. In addition to staying at least 25 yards (23 m) away from elk and bison, always stay at least 100 yards (91 m) away from bears and wolves.

data.description: On August 13, 2026 a brown bear entered camps and food caches in the Arrigetch Peaks area, obtaining food from a soft-sided, bag-type Bear Resistant Food Container (BRFC). At this time, we strongly recommend hard-sided BRFCs for all visitors to the Arrigetch Peaks area. Hard-sided BRFCs can be checked out at the Bettles Ranger Station. Backpackers in the area should maintain a high level of bear awareness and continue to follow best practices for camping in bear country.

data.title: Harmful Algal Blooms Occurring in Lake Richie and Intermediate Lake
data.description: Blooms are tested for toxin levels and monitored. Toxin levels are consistently low on Isle Royale. It is not recommended to filter water in any areas where there is surface scum, strong odors, or other evidence of a significant bloom. Blooms move around depending on wind and rain – filter water from places where blooms are not present or a different water source. It is low risk to filter water from relatively clear areas of an impacted water source.

data.description: Closures may occur due to inclement weather, construction projects, or other emergency conditions. Please visit the linked page for information about current closures.

data.title: Smokey air from local wildfires
data.description: Current air quality is being influenced by local fires and can change in an instant. Check https://www.airnow.gov/ for specific air quality index (AQI) information for your favorite spot at Lake Roosevelt National Recreation Area.

data.title: Lindenwald Opens for 2026 Season
data.description: Lindenwald Tours – 2026 Season Lindenwald is open for tours Friday–Sunday at 10 AM, 11 AM, 1 PM, and 3 PM. Tours are first-come, first-served. Monday–Thursday: grounds are open, but no tours are available. Park stamps, and restrooms are available in the Visitor Center.

data.title: Scam Warning: Book Ferry Tickets Through Authorized Concessioner Only
data.description: The National Park Service is aware of fraudulent websites selling invalid ferry tickets to Fort Sumter and Fort Moultrie National Historical Park. Valid ferry tickets can only be purchased through the park's authorized concessioner at www.fortsumtertours.com. Visitors should carefully verify the website address before purchasing tickets. Tickets purchased through unauthorized websites are not valid and will not be honored.

data.title: Construction on North Park Road
data.description: Construction underway on North Park Road between Leeks Marina and Lizard Creek Campground. 15-min delays both directions 6am-9pm / 1-hour delays both directions 9pm-6am. The section of road is about 7 miles north of Colter Bay and 11.5 miles south of Yellowstone.

data.title: Partial Beach Closures in Place in Front of Buxton Village
data.description: The beachfront in front of Buxton Village is temporarily closed due to the presence of threatened oceanfront structures and Dare County's beach nourishment project. Renourished sections of beach will open to the public immediately after construction activities conclude in the areas, generally within 24 hours.

data.title: Juniper Lake Campground Closed
data.description: The Juniper Lake Campground and day use area is currently closed for maintenance and campground improvement projects. Potable water is not available in the campground. The Juniper Lake Road (access to lake and trailheads) is open. Please drive with caution as road crews and contractors may be actively working along the roadway.

data.title: Alternate Route for Access to Root Glacier
data.description: The old route to access Root Glacier is no longer safe due to unstable ground. An alternative, new route exists past the Amazon Creek. Seek information at the visitor center or news release webpage.

data.title: Fire Restrictions
data.description: Due to the continued fire danger in Southern Oregon, Oregon Caves National Monument and Preserve has instituted a full fire ban. To ensure public safety and to provide the highest degree of protection to park resources, the Fire Ban prohibits Campfires. Wood and charcoal fires are NOT allowed in Oregon Caves National Monument and Preserve.

data.title: Dingmans Falls Trail, Road, and Access Closed for Bridge Replacement
data.description: Dingmans Falls site is closed for a bridge replacement project and trail rehabilitation. All traffic, including pedestrian, cyclist, and vehicle traffic, is prohibited on the road and trail during construction.

data.title: Construction Activity at Meyers Beach; Visitor and Kayak Access Maintained
data.description: Construction has begun on the Meyers Beach Access Path Project. Access to the beach and parking lot will remain open, but visitors should expect construction noise and closed lawn areas for staging. Kayak groups should move gear directly to the beach to reduce congestion. The project will upgrade the existing staircase to include a universally designed path, improving access to the beach and kayak launch for all visitors.

data.title: Stage 2 Burn Restrictions
data.description: All campfires are prohibited. Devices using pressurized liquid or gas (stoves, grills or lanterns) that include shut-off valves are permitted when used in an area at least three feet or more from flammable material such as grasses or pine needles. Smoking is only allowed in an enclosed vehicle.

data.title: Bridge to Maryland Heights & C&O Canal CLOSED
data.description: The NPS is rehabilitating the stairway connecting the Goodloe Byron Memorial Footbridge to the C&O Canal NHP towpath. The stairway will be CLOSED beginning July 27 for approximately one month while crews install the new stairwell. A shuttle will run between C&O Canal Lock 34 and Harpers Ferry National Historical Park Visitor Center. This will impact access to Maryland Heights, the Appalachian NST, and the Potomac Heritage NST.

data.title: Monsoon Season & Flash Floods
data.description: Heavy rains can cause sudden flooding, especially in canyons and washes. Do not drive or hike through flood waters. Get to high ground and wait for floods to subside. Some roads may close temporarily; closures are posted at the visitor center.

data.title: Trail update 7/25/26
data.description: Most trails are open and ready for the public. Those that remain closed are the Charleston Road/ Goudey Trail past the Cherokee Path and the portion of Cherokee Path between the stockade fort and the Charleston Road.

data.title: Bicycles and Pedestrians now allowed on Volcano Road
data.description: Capulin Volcano Highway is now a roadway shared by multiple users that include vehicles, hikers, bikers, walkers and runners. Dogs on a minimum 6-foot leash are also allowed on the roadway. Be watchful of others that are present on the highway. Follow the new traffic flow signs and keep vehicle and bicycle speeds at the posted speed limits of 20 mph in general and 10 mph in the S curves. Let’s all stay safe!

data.title: Trail Closure
data.description: A portion of the Headland Trail is closed due to ongoing restoration work. Access to the trail will now close at 2:30 pm daily. All hikers must be off the trails by 4:45 pm.

data.title: Temporary Emergency Fire Closure
data.description: Open fires of any kind, including charcoal fires, are prohibited until conditions improve. Smoking is prohibited except for in vehicles or buildings where indicated. Use of gas stoves is permitted in areas that are clear of flammable materials.

data.title: Visitor Center Open at 419 Decatur Street
data.description: The New Orleans Jazz NHP & Jean Lafitte NHP&P have a combined French Quarter Visitor Center at 419 Decatur Street. Open Tuesdays through Saturdays, 9:30 am to 4:30 pm. Calendar for events: https://www.nps.gov/jazz/planyourvisit/calendar.

data.title: Partial Trail Closure
data.description: The crossover trail through the center of the historic area, near the flagpole, is temporarily closed for safety. The remainder of the main park trail is open.

data.title: Harmful Algae Bloom
data.description: A Harmful Algae Bloom has been confirmed in recent water samples taken from the Nelson's Landing and the Cottonwood Cove areas on Lake Mohave. To reduce health risks, the National Park Service recommends recreators limit body contact with these waters when algae is present. Please click here for pictures of this dangerous cyanobacteria and contact the Park at 702-293-8990 for updates on this advisory.

data.title: Outer Island Nighttime Closure
data.description: Outer Island is closed to all use from 10 PM to 6 AM due to bear activity and food‑storage concerns. Day use is permitted outside these hours. The closure remains in effect until further notice to protect visitor safety and support ongoing wildlife management.

data.title: Upper Fort Mason Roads and Parking Area Closures Fall 2025 - Fall 2026
data.description: Roads and parking areas at upper Fort Mason will have closures during utilities and seismic retrofit projects. Closures planned Fall 2025 through Fall 2026. Lots will be fenced and used as staging areas for projects occurring at Fort Mason. Signs will be posted in advance of utilities work as project progresses through each area at Fort Mason. Read signs and do not park in posted areas. Vehicles will be towed at owner's expense.

relatedRoadEvents.title: Parking Closure of Fort Mason Lots Until December 2026

data.title: Construction for Seawall Project
data.description: Starting July 27, 2026, Castillo de San Marcos National Monument will begin construction to replace, raise and rehabilitate the park’s failing seawalls. The historic fort will remain accessible throughout the project. Some areas outside of the fort will be closed for safety.

data.title: Stockton Island Trail Access
data.description: The trail between Presque Isle Bay and Quarry Bay on Stockton Island is open, but a footbridge on the western portion of the trail was washed out in a 2024 storm. Visitors must wade through shallow water or take an alternate route.

data.title: Ongoing Closure Notices
data.description: Devils Island dock and campsites and West Bay Club on Sand Island are closed. These closures affect only a small portion of the Lakeshore. Enjoy your visit.

data.title: Visiting During Monsoon Season (July-September)
data.description: All park trails are closed for 30 minutes following any lightning strikes five miles or less from the park. This includes Montezuma Well and the trail to see Montezuma Castle. Please check the forecast ahead of your visit.

data.title: Visiting During Monsoon Season (July-September)
data.description: All park trails are closed for 30 minutes following any lightning strikes five miles or less from the park. This includes the Pueblo Trail and Tavasci Marsh Trail. Please check the forecast ahead of your visit.

data.title: Visitor Center Contact Phone Down
data.description: The Theodore Roosevelt Birthplace contact phone, (212) 260-1616, is currently experiencing issues. Rangers may not be able to receive your call. For questions, please email thrb_info@nps.gov.

data.title: No Water Available at Ok-A-Beh Marina - Flushing Restrooms Closed
data.description: Due to a water shortage, flushable toilets are currently unavailable at the Ok-A-Beh Marina. Vault toilets are available at the upper parking lot and a floating restroom is available on the courtesy dock.

data.title: Construction at Blow-Me-Down Mill
data.description: The area around the Blow-Me-Down Mill and Dam are temporarily closed through August due to work to repair and reinforce the foundation of the Blow-Me-Down Mill.

data.title: Construction Activity at Little Sand Bay; Boat and Kayak Access Maintained
data.description: Construction for the Little Sand Bay Marina Rehabilitation Project begins May 1. The Town of Russell boat launch and the NPS kayak beach will remain open, with short detours around work areas. Expect reduced parking, delays, and increased noise. The Little Sand Bay Visitor Center will be closed in 2026 due to construction.

data.title: Sculptor's Studio Heat Advisory
data.description: The Sculptor’s Studio may close temporarily during periods of high heat to protect visitors and staff. Please check with park staff upon arrival for the most up‑to‑date information on whether the Studio is open or closed.

data.title: Avoid Water Contact at Sand Beach Lagoon (Not for Sand Beach)
data.description: Bacterial levels have exceeded public health standards at Sand Beach Lagoon and a Public Health Advisory has been posted. The public is advised against swimming at this beach until bacterial levels return to healthful levels. (Not for Sand Beach.)

data.title: Bighorn Lake Elevation is Below 3625ft
data.description: When lake levels are below 3625, boaters are advised to avoid areas south of Horseshoe Bend and the South Narrows due to low water levels. Throughout the year, lake water levels fluctuate greatly. Hazards and launching abilities change with the water levels. Please use caution when recreating on Bighorn Lake.

data.title: Sections of moat wall closed until Winter 2026
data.description: Sections of the moat wall that were damaged by Hurricanes Helene and Milton (2024) are undergoing repair and reinforcement. For your safety, please follow posted signage and do not cross any barricades.

data.title: Fire Danger VERY HIGH
data.description: Wood-burning fires and charcoal grills are prohibited. Propane and gas stoves allowed only in campground and picnic areas for cooking food. No smoking on trail. No roadside parking. Fireworks are always prohibited.

data.title: Current Alerts and Conditions
data.description: Be sure to review the Alerts and Conditions below before and during your visit for additional, up-to-date information on closures, cautions, and other current park conditions.

data.title: Detour along Mount Vernon Trail at Gravelly Point
data.description: Due to constriction for the Long Bridge Project, the Mount Vernon Trail will be temporarily detoured around the construction zone beginning on July 15, 2026. Trail users should expect periodic crossings of equipment and materials where the trail meets the construction access road. Detour will be in place through 2030.

data.title: Fire Operations
data.description: Wildfires are occurring in the region. Water scooping airplanes are using the reservoir. Please use caution and stay clear of areas where water scooping operations are occurring.

data.title: Do not pick up hitchhikers
data.description: Do not pick up hitchhikers. Please report their locations to law enforcement by calling 911.

data.description: Avoid area around the church & under trees in high wind conditions

data.description: Our phone lines are working intermittently. If you are not able to reach us by phone, please email us at bela_information@nps.gov.

data.title: Roadway Work to Begin at Sanford Yake Campgournd Monday, July 13th
data.description: The National Park Service announces that Federal Highway Administration contractors will begin roadway and pavement maintenance at Sanford Yake Campground starting Monday, July 13, 2026. This project will include chip seal, micro seal, micro surfacing, and pavement striping throughout key areas of Lake Meredith National Recreation Area. Visitors to Alibates Flint Quarries National Monument and Lake Meredith National Recreation Area are encouraged to follow all posted message boards and traffic instructions.

data.title: Paving Work Ongoing Throughout the Park
data.description: Paving work is being done throughout Ozark National Scenic Riverways during the 2026 summer season, including at Alley Spring, Round Spring, Pulltite, and Big Spring. Watch here and on our park Facebook page for updates, as roads and campground loops may close and reopen depending on work progress.

data.title: Round Spring Pavilion Parking Area Closed
data.description: The parking lot for the Round Spring Pavilion and for Round Spring itself is CLOSED for the remainder of the 2026 summer season while the low water bridge over Spring Valley Creek is rebuilt. Alternative parking near Round Spring Group Campsites 4-8 will provide trail access to the north side of Round Spring.

data.title: Round Spring Lower River Landing Closed
data.description: The lower river landing at Round Spring, located in the campground, is closed until further notice for paving. Floaters putting in or taking out at Round Spring should plan to use the upper landing behind Carr's Store.

data.title: Total Fire Restrictions Implemented June 20, 2026
data.description: Due to extreme fire conditions, all fires at Lake Roosevelt National Recreation Area are prohibited effective 12:01 a.m., June 20, until further notice. No open flames are permitted. Only self-contained propane or gas cookstoves and lanterns are allowed during the full fire ban.

data.title: Stehekin is Open, Services Limited at Stehekin Landing
data.description: Visitor and recreational opportunities continue to be available in the Stehekin Valley. Some services are limited at the Stehekin Landing following flood damage in December 2025.

data.title: Mora Road Closed for Essential Repairs
data.description: Mora Road is closed to all traffic, including bicycles and pedestrians, at the campground. Rialto Beach is not accessible via Mora Road during this construction period. Mora Campground is open. This construction work will repair damage from a severe winter flood event, fortify the road against river migration, and protect long-term access to Rialto Beach.

data.title: Fort Jay front gate only — Temporary Closure.
data.description: The FRONT GATE of Fort Jay is temporarily closed to all. The fort is currently open to visitation Wednesday thru Sunday 10am to 4pm. Access to the fort will be via the western or rear sallyport.

data.title: Staircase Developed Area is Open, Use Caution in Burned Areas
data.description: The Staircase developed area is open. The surrounding wilderness areas will remain closed as repair and recovery efforts continue. Use extreme caution when entering burned areas. Burned landscapes may contain falling trees and branches, loose boulders, unstable ground, stump holes, landslides, and debris flows. Changing conditions such as wind, rain, or storms can rapidly trigger hazards. Learn more on our Fire Conditions and Updates page.

data.title: Partial Closures to Little Calumet River Trail and Glenwood Dunes Trail
data.description: Marquette Greenway construction will require closing sections of the Glenwood Dunes Trail (April–December 2026) and Little Calumet River / Mnoké Prairie Trail (May–December 2026). Closure dates may shift as work progresses. Please follow all posted closures and check the park website or NPS App for updates.

data.title: Munising Falls Trail Closed Until Further Notice
data.description: The Munising Falls Trail within Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore is closed until further notice. Approximately 75-feet of the paved trail was washed out April 28th from recent heavy rainfall and seasonal snow melt.

data.title: Church Loop Trail Closure
data.description: The Church Loop Trail in the Thurmond area of the park is temporarily closed due to downed trees.

data.title: Stage 2 fire restrictions in effect
data.description: No setting, building, maintaining, attending, or using open fires of any kind in the park. This includes campfires and charcoal fires in Watchman Campground, South Campground, and picnic areas in Zion Canyon. Stoves fueled by petroleum or liquid propane gas are allowed. Smoking is prohibited, except within an enclosed vehicle.

data.title: Stage II Fire Restrictions in effect - campfires banned
data.description: Stage II Fire Restrictions are in effect at Great Basin National Park. Due to extreme fire danger, campfires, charcoal grills, and outdoor smoking are prohibited throughout the park. Gas and liquid-fueled stoves are permitted.

data.title: Food Storage Regulations in Effect
data.description: Proper food storage is required on Isle Royale. All food, trash, scented items, cooking supplies, cooking utensils, and fish/fish parts must be stored properly. To learn more about food storage and to learn how to properly store your food, trash, and scented items, click "more."

data.title: Biscuit Basin Closed Due to Hydrothermal Explosion
data.description: The parking lot, boardwalk, and Firehole River at Biscuit Basin, located north of Old Faithful, is closed to all travel until further notice due to the possibility of another event at the site of a hydrothermal explosion that occurred July 23, 2024.

relatedRoadEvents.title: Biscuit Basin Closed Due to Hydrothermal Explosion

data.title: Arlington House Potential Closures
data.description: Due to HVAC system issues, Arlington House may close to visitors when interior temperatures reach 85°F. Temporary closures may occur with little notice to protect the safety and comfort of visitors and staff.

data.title: East Rim Drive is CLOSED from Park Headquarters to Phantom Ship Overlook
data.description: East Rim Drive is currently CLOSED to all public access from Park Headquarters to Phantom Ship Overlook for road construction. West Rim Drive, North Entrance Road, East Rim Drive from North Junction to Phantom Ship Overlook, Cloudcap Road, and Pinnacles Road are now OPEN for travel.

relatedRoadEvents.title: East Rim Drive from Park HQ to Phantom Ship Overlook is currently CLOSED for road construction.

data.title: Mainland Museum Closure
data.description: The Cumberland Island Museum will be closed for an extended period due to roof leakages. We apologize for any inconvenience but look forward to reopening to you in the future.

data.title: Partial Trail Closure at Portage Lakefront and Riverwalk
data.description: Closed portion of Portage Lakefront and Riverwalk Trail along Burns Waterway due to unsafe conditions from erosional damage. This trail portion will remain closed while funding is sought for repair work. Pier access remains open on either side of closure.

data.title: Wood & Charcoal Burn Ban
data.description: To protect park infrastructure and visitors during this hot, dry period of year, wood and charcoal/briquette burning is temporarily banned. Propane grills are still okay. Thank you for recreating responsibly in your national recreation area.

data.title: A Fire Ban (Stage 2 Fire Restrictions) Are In Effect
data.description: Due to very high fire danger, the extended weather forecast, and current fire activity in the State of Colorado, Stage 2 Fire Restrictions are now in effect within Rocky Mountain National Park. When Stage 2 Fire Restrictions are in effect, this means that all campfires, including charcoal briquette fires are not permitted anywhere within Rocky Mountain National Park. This ban is effective beginning today, June 29, and will remain in effect until further notice.

data.title: Be cautious around park rivers & learn how to cross safely!
data.description: Many hikers underestimate the power of moving water. Regardless of your knowledge, skills, and experience use these pointers in making wise decisions before attempting to cross a river.

data.description: Be sure to review the Alerts and Conditions below before and during your visit for additional, up-to-date information on closures, cautions, and other current park conditions.

data.title: Park Headquarters Road is closed
data.description: Park Headquarters Road is closed due to rehabilitation work on the Sugarlands water and wastewater systems.

data.title: Two Medicine North Shore Trailhead Reroute
data.description: In 2026, Two Medicine's North Shore Trailhead is not accessible due to construction in the Two Medicine Campground. A reroute has been established to access the North Shore Trail but does require a ford (unbridged water crossing). Directional signage is in place marking the reroute. Hikers may also access Twin Falls, Upper Two Medicine Lake, No Name Lake, and Dawson Pass without a ford, by using the South Shore Trail. Note: this adds approximately 1 mile of distance, one-way.

data.title: Critical Backcountry Updates/Closures
data.description: Visit this link for the inner canyon weather forecast, current trail closures, today's heat risk, and drinking water availability.

data.title: Parkwide Fire Ban in effect until further notice beginning June 26
data.description: Beginning Friday 6/26/26 until rescinded, a parkwide fire ban is implemented for all campfires & the ignition of wood, briquettes, or any fuel in fire pits, fire pans, & BBQ grills.

data.title: Big South Fork’s Brewster Bridge Road to Temporarily Close for Repair
data.description: Brewster Bridge Road in Big South Fork NRRA will temporarily close for repair and re-pavement beginning on Monday, June 29. The road was heavily damaged from significant rain events in 2022 and 2023. The area boat launch and day use area will be inaccessible during the project.

data.title: Campfire Ban in All Portions of the Park Complex Begins June 29
data.description: Effective Monday, June 29, campfires or the ignition of wood, briquettes, or any fuel in fire pits, fire pans, and barbeque grills, are banned in all portions of North Cascades National Park Service Complex, which includes North Cascades National Park, Ross Lake National Recreation Area, and Lake Chelan National Recreation Area.. This applies to anything that produces ash, including charcoal grills. Propane fire pits are not allowed during the ban.

data.title: Patriots Point Ferries Accessibility Information
data.description: Ferries to Fort Sumter from Patriots Point are not always accessible for individuals who use mobility assistance devices or have trouble navigating stairs. The Fort Sumter Visitor Center departure location is fully accessible or visitors can call Fort Sumter Tours (843-722-2628) for current Patriots Point accessibility conditions.

data.title: Going-to-the-Sun Road is Open for 2026 Season
data.description: The Going-to-the-Sun Road is fully open for the 2026 summer season. The road may now be accessed by motorized vehicles over Logan Pass from both the West Glacier and St. Mary Entrances.

data.title: Please use caution when visiting park grounds.
data.description: Park grounds and walking paths are accessible but visitors should use caution as there are fallen trees, stumps, and other typhoon debris.

data.title: Death Canyon Trailhead Construction Closure
data.description: Death Canyon Road and Trailhead are closed to all use. Start hikes at alternative trailheads such as Granite Canyon, LSR Preserve, and Taggart Lake.

data.title: Limited access to areas at Asan Beach.
data.description: Due to the impacts of Typhoon Sinlaku, areas of Asan Beach remain inaccessible. Visitors should use caution when walking to the beach area and stay out of damaged areas.

data.title: Talisman-Barrett Beach Dock Closed for 2026 Season; Services Limited
data.description: Due to damage from winter ice, the Talisman-Barrett Beach dock is closed. NPS staff are evaluating options for repairs. There is no timeline for restoration. Boaters should plan to anchor in the bay to access the site. Be advised that the area is extremely shallow. Restroom maintenance will be limited during this time and visitors must pack out all trash and belongings. Public use of some areas will be restricted for safety.

data.title: Delays along Highway 101
data.description: There are multiple traffic stops along Highway 101 from Orick, CA to Crescent City, CA due to road construction. Extra time may be needed to travel throughout the park. Delay times may vary. Please stay alert and drive cautiously.

data.title: Ryan Visitor Center Phone Line Out of Service
data.description: The Floyd Bennett Field Ryan Visitor Center phone line (718-338-3799) is out of service. For information on ranger programs in the Jamaica Bay Unit, call the Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge Visitor Center at 718-318-4340. For questions about permits, events, or other park information, call the general park information line at 718-354-4606. For emergencies, call U.S. Park Police's 24-hour dispatch at 718-354-4700.

data.title: Barataria Visitor Center and Trails are Closed
data.description: Because of upcoming demolition and construction of the trails and Visitor Center, all trails at the Barataria Preserve and the Visitor Center are closed, with the exception of Twin Canals Trail. This is a day-use area only with no restrooms. Visitor services are relocated to the Wetlands Education Center and trails at 4917 City Park Drive, Jean Lafitte, 70067. Rangers will be on site Wednesdays and Thursdays 10 am to 2 pm for programming and ranger talks at the Town of Lafitte's Civic Center.

data.title: Battery 234 Loop Road Closure
data.description: The Battery 234 Loop Road and Battery Cooper within the GUIS, Fort Pickens Management Area will be closed to all for vehicle, bicyclists, and foot (pedestrian) traffic until further notice for safety purposes until the park can correct the leaning and structurally unstable historic Tower 234 that poses danger to visitors and staff. The beach access points for pedestrians from the Gulf (south) side will also be closed. The pipe gates at the entrance and exit points will be locked with accompanied signage.

data.title: Broken Windsock at Serpentine Hot Springs
data.description: The windsock at the Serpentine Hot Springs airstrip is broken, and the National Park Service is in the process of ordering a replacement. At this time, we do not have an estimated date for when it will be reinstalled. Please use caution when utilizing the airstrip.

data.title: Glenmont Heat Advisory
data.description: The house at Glenmont is currently experiencing high heat conditions. As a result, house tours may be abbreviated or canceled due to safety concerns.

data.title: Hot Conditions
data.description: Limit strenuous hiking to early morning and late evening hours. Expect temperatures in the High Peaks and Chalone Peak to be at least 10 degrees hotter than parking areas. Drink plenty of water and carry at least one liter of water for each hour of hiking. Bring salty snacks, a hat, and sunscreen for the hike. Know the signs and symptoms of heat related illnesses. In case of a heat related emergency get to a cool place and seek help immediately.

data.title: Reds Meadow Road Access Restrictions in 2026
data.description: Reds Meadow Road remains under construction in 2026 and will be closed Monday through Friday from June 13 through July 1, then Monday through Wednesday from July 2 through September 20, then Monday through Friday starting September 21.

data.title: Being Prepared for Excessive Heat & Humidity
data.description: Congaree can be hot & humid from late spring through early fall. Be sure that you & your party (including pets) have adequate water & choose activities that fit your level of physical fitness. Consider visiting early in the morning when it is cooler.

data.title: Fire restrictions in place

data.title: EV charging station unavailable

data.title: Photo Season
data.description: Just a reminder as the weather is starting to get nice, and people are thinking about where to take graduation, wedding, prom or formal, pregnancy, birthday, and any other type of photography or filming! data.title: Large vehicle restrictions now in effect for Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway
data.description: As of June 7, 2026, the park is enforcing size and weight limits for vehicles on the Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway. Vehicles that exceed length, width, height, or weight limits cannot travel between Canyon Junction and the park's East Entrance. See the current limits on the page linked below.

data.title: Road workers on Park Road in Davis Bayou
data.description: Phase II of the Davis Bayou Bicycle and Pedestrian Path is in process. Visitors may encounter minor traffic delays and flaggers on Eagle Point and Park Road.

data.title: Fredericksburg Battlefield Visitor Center Closed, Store and Grounds Open
data.description: Starting November 20, 2025 the Fredericksburg Battlefield Visitor Center will be closed while updates are made to building systems. Front Desk operations including visitor orientation will move to the adjacent Fredericksburg Battlefield Bookstore. The Chancellorsville Visitor Center remains open to visitors 9am - 5pm all week.

data.title: No Potable Water in Park Campgrounds
data.description: There currently is no water available in any campground in Great Basin National Park.  Water is available at the RV Fill and Dump Station, the Great Basin, and the Lehman Caves Visitor Center as well as some local businesses.

data.title: Your GPS May Be Wrong
data.description: There are five entrances to the park. GPS may take you to the wrong entrance or attempt to follow the most direct route, which could lead to closed gates. It can take hours to reroute to the correct entrance. Check directions & maps, not just your GPS.

data.title: Expect long lines at entrances on weekends.
data.description: Lengthy delays are likely at the southwest park entrance on SR706 on weekends. Check Google Maps for backup (represented by the orange/red line) at link below. Please do not block driveways or roads while in line outside the park.

data.title: Kaymoor Miners Trail Closure
data.description: From June 15 through November 19 the upper part of the Kaymoor Miners Trail (from Kaymoor Top down to the mine site at the junction with the Kaymoor Trail) will be closed Monday through Thursday due to a trail rehab project. The trail is expected to be fully open Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.

data.title: Heavy Traffic and High Visitation Alert
data.description: Pinnacles experiences extremely high visitation on weekends, holidays, and during favorable weather, especially in the spring. Expect long lines and delays between 10:00 am and 3:00 pm. If you're planning to hike the High Peaks, Condor Gulch, Balconies, or Moses Spring Trail, it’s recommended to arrive before 8:00 am (parking may fill earlier). Additionally, campground access may be temporarily delayed during peak periods of visitation when ALL incoming traffic is held.

data.title: Accessing Fort Barrancas
data.description: Fort Barrancas is open 9 am–4 pm Wednesday through Sunday. To access Fort Barrancas, visitors will need to enter the Naval Air station Pensacola through the west gate.

data.title: For entrance fees, we accept digital passes and credit/debit cards
data.description: Digital passes or credit/debit cards are the ONLY method of payment at all fee collection areas. Pre-paid digital passes are available online and may be purchased in advance.

data.title: Roadwork may cause delays on US 41/Tamiami Trail
data.description: Current roadwork is ongoing along the park's northern boundary on US Highway 41/Tamiami Trail to raise the road for Everglades Restoration benefits. Drivers may experience up to 15-minute delays and should watch for personnel, equipment and slow downs.

data.title: Group Reservations
data.description: Groups of 11 or more people should contact the Visitor Center at ADAM_Visitor_Center@nps.gov or 617-770-1175 at least two weeks in advance to arrange their visit.

data.title: Jacob Riis Park Access Restrictions
data.description: Due to extremely hazardous conditions Gateway National Recreation Area has restricted access to sections of Jacob Riis Park. Erosion has created unsafe conditions from Bays 1-5, and portions of the eastern beach are closed.

data.title: Do Not Handle Wildlife
data.description: If you see a dead bat or a bat acting strangely at the fort, please do not touch or move it. Report the location of the animal to park staff.

data.title: Annual Summer Closures and Restrictions in Effect
data.description: The 49 Palms trail along with some campgrounds, facilities, and areas have adjusted availability during the summer. For the full list of changes, please visit our Summer Closures page.

data.title: Upper and Lower Plaza Rehabilitation
data.description: The Plazas, Rotunda, and the Observation Deck of the Memorial will be inaccessible for the 2026 and 2027 seasons due to the Upper and Lower Plaza Rehabilitation. The visitor center and grounds will remain open. Thank you for your understanding.

data.title: Passenger Ferry Dock Closed; Visitors Deboard via Beach Landing
data.description: The ferry dock servicing the Cape Lookout Lighthouse area is closed for repairs. Visitors will deboard the ferry in front of the lighthouse. To reach the boardwalk, visitors will need to walk 5–10 minutes on soft sand. Depending on the tide, visitors may also need to walk through water.

data.title: Lake Powell Recreational Water Advisory
data.description: Any time that you do recreational activities (swimming, water skiing, making sand castles, etc.) on the beaches or in the waters of Lake Powell you are strongly encouraged to follow basic hygiene practices. A number of conditions can cause potential water quality issues on Lake Powell, at Lees Ferry, and on Colorado River tributaries.

data.title: Closures: Detours; Towpath; Points of Interest
data.description: Multiple items are closed due to hazardous conditions or maintenance. See below for more details.

data.title: Cades Cove Loop Road is closed to motor vehicles every Wednesday
data.description: Cades Cove Loop Road is closed to motor vehicles every Wednesday through September 30. This allows pedestrians and cyclists to enjoy the cove without the presence of vehicles on the roadway.

data.title: Road Construction
data.description: Far View Sites and Cedar Tree Tower are closed for road improvements. Road work along the first four miles of the park road from the entrance station will begin in early summer. Delays of up to 30 minutes are possible - please check the park map before your visit. Wetherill Mesa Road has compacted gravel for 30 feet; motorcycles should take extra caution on this road.

data.title: Major road construction on Hwy 199
data.description: Travelers using Highway 199 between Crescent City and Cave Junction should expect multiple traffic delays beginning as early as May due to ongoing Caltrans construction. For the most current delay and closure information—including upcoming four‑hour full closures—please check the Caltrans District 1 Road Information Bulletin for updates and follow their social media channels.

data.title: Bacteria Levels at Arizona Hot Springs
data.description: Fecal bacteria in water samples taken from Arizona Hot Springs frequently reach high levels, which can transmit human diseases. To reduce health risks, the National Park Service recommends recreators limit body contact in these waters, clean after use, and to never put your head under water at hot springs. Please contact the Park at 702-293-8990 for updates on this advisory.

data.title: Navigation
data.description: Please do not rely upon GPS digital navigation systems to find your way to Craters of the Moon. Please note that the Robert Limbert Visitor Center at 1266 Craters Loop Road is located just off U.S. Highway 20/26/93 and is not accessed via any unpaved roads.

data.title: Denali Park Road Information
data.description: In summer, the Denali Park Road is open to Mile 15 (Savage River) for personal vehicles. Vehicle travel further into the park is limited to transit and tour buses.

data.title: 2026 Tour Season
data.description: Visit https://www.nps.gov/adam/planyourvisit/2026-tour-season.htm for details on the 2026 tour season, including operating hours and tour offerings. The Visitor Center is open 9am-5pm Wednesdays-Sundays. The historic homes are open Wednesdays-Sundays. Entrance fees required for entry into historic homes. Guided tour reservations are available first-come, first-served on the day of the tour at the Visitor Center. Reservations not required for self-guided tours.

data.title: Stoplight In Use due to Limited Parking
data.description: Limited Parking at the Visitor Center is monitored by the use of a Stoplight. This light helps meter traffic so that parking spots are available for visitors. Stoplight generally in effect from 10 am to 4 pm. Wait times vary daily.

data.title: Note About Using GPS for Directions
data.description: Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park is located at 72 McBride Avenue Extension, Paterson, NJ 07501. Use this full address when searching using a GPS device or map app or use GPS coordinates N40.91533° W74.17992°

data.title: Yaqui Ridge Trail Closure
data.description: Due to nearby construction and blasting, the 1-mile Yaqui Ridge Trail is closed starting April 13, 2026 until further notice to ensure visitor safety. The closure begins at the junction with Joe’s Canyon Trail, and access beyond this point is not permitted. This affects access to the southern terminus of the Arizona National Scenic Trail.

data.title: Sheep Hunting Closure
data.description: The Federal Subsistence Board closed sheep hunting to all users on Federal public lands within Yukon-Charley Rivers National Preserve and Glacier Mountain Controlled Use Areas Units in 20E and 25C due to significant declines to the sheep population. The authority was granted via WP26-76 on April 24, 2026 and the closure with extend through June 30, 2028.

data.title: Backcountry route open to vehicles May 15 - November 15
data.description: Valles Caldera's backcountry road system opens to vehicles on Friday, May 15, 2026. Forty vehicles passes will be issued per day through November 15, when the route closes for the 2026 season. Passes may be reserved up to 3 months in advance at Recreation.gov. Any remaining daily passes will be available on a first come, first served basis in the Volcano Discovery Center.

data.title: Janis-Ziegler House (Green Tree Tavern) Closed
data.description: The Janis-Ziegler House (Green Tree Tavern) building is currently closed, due to unsafe conditions. Other park buildings and grounds are open according to regular schedules. For program information, please check with park staff at the Ste. Genevieve Welcome Center, 573-880-7189.

data.title: Seasonal Trail Closures Due to Extreme Heat May 15 – September 30
data.description: Goldstrike Canyon, Arizona Hot Springs, Liberty Bell Arch, White Rock Canyon, and Lone Palm trails will be closed for visitor and first responder safety. Please check the park website, social media, and weather for updates before visiting. Arizona, Goldstrike, and Lone Palm hot springs remain open and accessible by water.

data.title: Prescribed Burn on Monday, May 11
data.description: The prescribed burn for May 11 has concluded and the Circle Trail is now open to visitors.

data.title: Fort Spokane Museum and Visitor Center to Close for Repairs
data.description: The Fort Spokane Museum and Visitor Center in Lake Roosevelt National Recreation Area is temporarily closed for the duration of the summer for critical historic preservation repairs. Dating to 1880, the landmark building originally served as the fort's guardhouse and now operates as the primary hub to introduce visitors to the park and its many resources.

data.title: Intermittent Road Closures During Utility Improvement Project
data.description: Beginning May 11, Stones River National Battlefield will implement intermittent road closures to support a utility improvement project by Middle Tennessee Electric. The park expects intermittent closures to continue for four months, depending on weather and construction conditions. Temporary closures and traffic impacts will occur in work areas along Thompson Lane and nearby sections of the battlefield. Visitors should expect intermittent disruptions and follow posted signs and staff directions.

data.title: Temporary Closure of Right Lane of Clara Barton Parkway
data.description: Temporary Closure of the Clara Barton Parkway Right Lane at Site 17, wooded areas between C&O Canal and Lock 10 parking lot, north to Lock 14, required to address ongoing safety concerns from DC Water emergency sanitary sewer overflow & bypass and pipe repair operations. Click on "More" below for specifica details on the closure.

data.title: Elevator for Accessible Tour Out of Service
data.description: Due to mechanical issues with the cave elevator, the Accessible Tour is currently unavailable. Please check back for updates or call the visitor center at (270) 758-2180.

data.title: Isaac Potts House (Washington's Headquarters) Closed For Restoration
data.description: The Isaac Potts House (Washington's Headquarters at Valley Forge) is temporarily closed for a restoration project. The Washington's Headquarters area, including the Valley Forge Train Station and exhibits, Commander-In-Chief's Guard Huts, and George Washington statue, remains open and accessible during regular operating hours. Learn more about the restoration project at the link below.

data.title: Historic Andrew Johnson Homestead Reopens
data.description: The Home of our 17th president has reopened to the public. Daily tours available. See GUIDED TOURS information on website for more details.

data.title: Change in Hours for Summer Season
data.description: Due to the potential of excessive summer heat, starting Monday May 4, The Lower Cliff Dwelling Trail will close at 12:00P.M. The visitor center & park will remain open until 4:00P.M. These hours will be in place until Saturday October 3.

data.title: Road Construction Work to begin May 4-Oct 24, 2026
data.description: Road construction to occur Monday through Friday between the hours of 7:00 am and 8:00 pm, weather permitting. Expect delays of up to 30 minutes during active construction periods.

data.title: Road Construction Work to begin May 4-October 24
data.description: Road construction work to occur Monday thru Friday between the hours of 7:00 am and 8:00 pm, weather permitting. Expect delays of up to 30 minutes during active construction periods.

data.title: Saint-Gaudens NHP is cashless
data.description: Cash payments at Saint-Gaudens NHP are not accepted as a method of payment for entry passes. Credit and debit cards are accepted.

data.title: Visitor Center and Bookstore Open Tues - Sun
data.description: Visitor Center and Bookstore hours are Tues - Sun 9-5. It is currently a .7 mile hike from the main parking lot and a .4 mile walk to the historic area from the Hikers Lot. Please keep this in mind. If you have access needs, please call the number posted in the parking lot.

data.title: Old Mine Road North Construction Closure Begins April 6, 2026
data.description: Old Mine Road between Jager Road and Route 206 will close to all traffic beginning on April 6, 2026. Contractors will work to rehabilitate a 3.5-mile stretch of road. The construction area will be closed to all traffic for the safety of park visitors and contractors.

relatedRoadEvents.title: Old Mine Road Between Jager Road and Route 206

data.title: Off Road Vehicle Inspections
data.description: ORV renewals & new permits will be issued at the Nathanial P. Reed Visitor Center Friday-Monday, 9am-1:30pm. No permits will be issued Tuesday-Thursday. Permits will be issued first-come first-served. Visit our ORV page for more information

data.title: ORV Permits Sold Online
data.description: Starting May 1st, 2026 ORV permits will be able to be purchased online. The physical office will remain open for the summer Friday-Monday from 9am-1:30pm. Please click the link to PREVIEW the site until it goes live on May 1st.

data.title: Infrastructure Improvements to Old Rag Trailhead
data.description: Effective May 4, Shenandoah National Park will begin infrastructure enhancements at the Old Rag Trailhead main parking lot. We expect to complete work by November 2026. Until then, the main parking lot is closed to all vehicle and pedestrian traffic. Visitors can access Old Rag Trailhead via existing overflow parking lots. Day-use tickets are still required from March 1 through November 30 in addition to a park entrance fee.

data.title: Shenandoah National Park Moved to Fully Cashless Fee Collection
data.description: On July 1, 2025, the park transitioned to a fully cashless system at our fee entrance stations. Only credit cards, debit cards, or mobile payments will be accepted.

data.title: Temporary Closure of Right Lane of Clara Barton Parkway
data.description: Temporary Closure of the Clara Barton Parkway Right Lane at Site 17, wooded areas between C&O Canal and Lock 10 parking lot, north to Lock 14, required to address ongoing safety concerns from DC Water emergency sanitary sewer overflow & bypass and pipe repair operations. Click on "More" below for specific details on the closure.

data.title: Ongoing Road Repair on Main Road
data.description: Ongoing road work will be taking place throughout the Main Road on the island. Expect potentially heavier vehicle traffic and areas of uneven terrain. Please yield to construction traffic. Be aware of approaching traffic both in front as well as from behind.

data.title: Paddling Conditions
data.description: Trees down across Cedar Creek between Bannister's Bridge and South Cedar Creek may require significant portages depending on water levels & paddlers should plan accordingly. All paddlers should have necessary equipment, including the 10 Essentials.

data.title: Cashless Operations
data.description: Black Canyon's operations are now cashless. South Rim Campground is by reservation only via Recreation.gov. East Portal & North Rim campground sites are first-come first-served and accept payment using Scan & Pay through Recreation.gov's mobile app.

data.title: Site Closure for Utilities Improvement Project
data.description: The Edgar Allan Poe National Historic Site is closed for a utilities improvement project.

data.title: Oversized Vehicles are Unable to Park in Visitor Center Parking Lot
data.description: Due to construction, oversized vehicles will not be allowed to park in the visitor center parking lot due to lack of space and ability to turn-around safely. There is oversized parking along the main park road.

data.title: Cleetwood Cove Trail is CLOSED for Rehabilitation
data.description: The Cleetwood Cove Trail is CLOSED for construction. This critical project will fully rehabilitate the trail and marina to ensure safe access to the lake, provide a much-improved visitor experience, and protect the environment.

data.title: Protect Yourself from Volcanic Tephra
data.description: Volcanic ash, rock and glassy strands (tephra) is present at Kīlauea summit and can irritate your skin, eyes and respiratory system. For your safety, do not handle it. Eye protection, long sleeves, long pants, a hat, closed-toe shoes and a dust mask are recommended.

data.title: Kīlauea eruption
data.description: Volcanic eruptions can be hazardous. Stay out of closed areas and monitor air quality. Eruptions can last a few hours and are often separated by pauses lasting several weeks.

data.title: Ohanapecosh Campground area closed for construction in 2026.
data.description: The entire Ohanapecosh Campground area is CLOSED for the duration of the construction project, including all campsites, visitor center, restrooms, picnic area, & Ohanapecosh river access.

data.title: Nature Center and Planetarium Closure
data.description: The Nature Center and Planetarium building is closed until further notice due to continued remediation. Check the park's calendar for changes to ranger programs and locations.

data.title: No dock access to Rainbow Bridge
data.description: At current lake levels, Rainbow Bridge docks do not reach the land. Dock-to-trail access to Rainbow Bridge will not be available until water levels rise again. Restrooms at the dock will remain open. This alert will stay up until the situation changes. Check the link for current lake information.

data.title: Hawk Creek Area Closed for 2026 Recreation Season
data.description: The Hawk Creek Campground and boat launch area will close to all public access starting April 16 through Oct. 6. The closure is necessary to keep visitors, staff, and construction crews safe during the Hawk Creek Road Improvements and Stabilization Project. It may be extended through Oct. 30, if needed. The project, managed by the Federal Highway Administration in partnership with Lincoln County and the National Park Service, will begin at the intersection of Hawk Creek Road and Miles Creston Road.

data.title: Operating Hours
data.description: The seashore is currently operating on the hours of 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM. Last entry into the seashore is at 7:00 pm.

data.title: Road Construction Near the Park
data.description: There is road construction near the park visitor center along 111th St. and S. Cottage Avenue. Please use caution and allow extra travel time when visiting. Construction is expected to last through the fall. In addition, on occasion the vehicle entrance for parking at 610 E. 111th street is limited to one lane.

data.title: Dogs Prohibited on Grand Parade Trails from April 1 to September 15
data.description: The Grand Parade Trails are closed to dogs from April 1 to September 15 to protect breeding birds nesting in the meadows. Nesting songbirds see dogs as predators, which can stress the birds and lead to less productive or even failed nests.

data.title: Aid Box Rock Climbing Area Closed
data.description: The Aid Box rock climbing area is temporarily closed due to a recent rock topple.

data.title: Theodore Roosevelt National Park moves to cashless fee collection
data.description: Starting May 1, Theodore Roosevelt National Park will accept only credit cards, debit cards, or digital payments for entrance fees, campground fees, and Interagency Passes. Cash and check payments will no longer be accepted.

data.title: Presidio Trust Trails Annual Coyote Pupping Season is April to October
data.description: To prevent dog-coyote conflicts, avoid seasonally closed sections of the Park Trail and the Bay Area Ridge Trail to dog walking. Explore open dog-friendly trails instead and remember to keep dogs on leash. Visit the Presidio Trust's website for more details.

data.title: Alava Trail Closure
data.description: The Mount Alava trail and Fatifati trail from the Fagasa pass to the summit is closed for trail improvement work until further notice. Visitors can hike to the Alava trail from the Old Vatia trail, it is a much steeper and more rugged climb. Other suggested hiking alternatives include Upper and Lower Sauma trails and the Tuafanua trail.

data.title: Launch Ramp Updates
data.description: Lake level changes will influence the functionality of all launch ramps. Find updated status of all launch ramps at the link.

data.title: Beat the Heat!
data.description: Make sure to take weather into consideration when visiting. Carry water and use sunscreen to reduce the risk of heat injuries during your visit.

data.title: Dead Horse Bay (Brooklyn) Remains Closed to the Public
data.description: The entire southern area of Dead Horse Bay, including Glass Bottle Beach, is closed to the public. Dead Horse Bay is located in Brooklyn, NYC.

data.title: Oasis of Mara Trail Partial Closure
data.description: Due to a heavy flooding event, the Oasis of Mara Trail is closed past the Oasis.

data.title: Traffic Delays - Gardner River High Bridge
data.description: Expect a single lane of traffic with up to 15-minute delays, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, from April 1 through late October 2026. Oversized/overweight vehicles (8'6"+ wide, 75'+ long, 80,000 lbs+ gross vehicle weight) will not be able to cross the bridge during this time.

relatedRoadEvents.title: Traffic Delays - Gardner River High Bridge

data.title: Trip-planning tips for 2026
data.description: Planning to visit Arches this year? To ensure the best experience, please anticipate potentially long wait times at the entrance station. If trailhead parking is full, plan to return a little later. Please avoid parking on vegetation and roadways to help preserve this beautiful place for everyone to enjoy.

data.title: Scam Warning - Book ferry tickets through concessioner site only
data.description: Valid ferry tickets can only be purchased through the website www.cumberlandislandferry.com. Check site carefully before purchasing. Only valid tickets will be honored.

data.title: Trip-planning tips for 2026
data.description: Planning to visit Canyonlands this year? To ensure the best experience, please anticipate potentially long wait times at the entrance station. If overlook or trailhead parking is full, plan to return a little later. Please avoid parking on vegetation and roadways to help preserve this beautiful place for everyone to enjoy.

data.title: Phone Service Unavailable
data.description: Phone service at Puʻukoholā Heiau National Historic Site is currently unavailable. If you need to contact the park, please email us at puhe_info@nps.gov and a staff member will respond as soon as possible. We appreciate your patience while service is being restored.

data.title: Telephone System is Experiencing Connectivity Issues
data.description: The phone system at Sagamore Hill is experiencing connectivity issues. Please contact the park via email at sahi_information@nps.gov when phones are out of service.

data.title: Temporary Closures of Park Entrance Possible if Parking Lots Become Full
data.description: If parking lots become full, there will be a temporary closure of the park entrance at Georgetown Pike & Old Dominion Drive. The park entrance will re-open as soon as space becomes available. For updated information about parking, call Visitor Center at 703-757-3101

data.title: Rehabilitation of Colonial Parkway Continues
data.description: Construction on the Colonial Parkway is affecting travel in many sections. Please follow all detour and caution signs. Additional information can be found at the link below.

data.title: Annual and lifetime passes not available for purchase
data.description: Annual and lifetime passes are not currently available for purchase at Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau National Historical Park. As an alternative, you can purchase an annual pass online.

data.title: DC Water Sewer Overflow
data.description: DC Water is managing a sanitary sewer overflow from the Potomac Interceptor near Lock 10. Anyone with questions or in need of support can reach out to DC Water’s 24-Hour Command Center at (202) 612-3400 or visit https://www.dcwater.com/about-dc-water/media/potomac-interceptor-collapse.

data.title: The Painted Desert Oasis Gift Shop, Gas Station and Restaurant are Open!
data.description: The Painted Desert Oasis gift shop, gas station and restaurant located at the north entrance of the park are open, and restrooms are available during construction. Visitor center operations are currently located at the Painted Desert Inn, two miles past the entrance station.

data.title: Parking impacted due to the Legacy Restoration Fund Project
data.description: The Lower Farm parking lot near the Mule Barn is closed due to the Legacy Restoration Fund Project. The Upper parking lot located near the Orangery has reduced capacity due to a partial closure because of the Legacy Restoration Fund Project. To learn more about parking at Hampton NHS, click the link or visit the alerts page and then scroll down to the area that talks about parking.

data.title: Park Headquarters Phones are Down
data.description: Phones at park headquarters are currently down. Please call the visitor center at Painted Desert Inn 928-235-2467 or the Visitor Services office 928-235-2391 between 8 am and 5 pm. You can also send us an email at pefo_information@nps.gov.

data.title: Illinois Memorial Closed for Restoration
data.description: The memorial itself closed for restoration starting on September 16, 2025. Starting on March 2, 2026, access to Tour Stops 2 and 3 will be temporarily closed. The closure point will be at the Shirley House. Visitors will still be able to continue north along Union Avenue and access the remainder of the Tour Road. This section will remain closed for the duration of the Illinois Memorial Restoration. The project is expected to be completed by September 2026.

data.title: Condition of Turkey Creek Trail
data.description: The South Turkey Creek Trail, located near the Harbor Bay Campground Area, is currently open for hiking for the first mile; however, the remainder of the trail is underwater and cannot be safely accessed.

data.title: Overlook Park Lot Unavailable After Dark
data.description: The park parking lot at 72 McBride Extension is open from dawn to dusk every day. Any vehicles left in the parking lot after dusk (i.e. sunset) are subject to towing at owner's expense.

data.title: Speed Limits are Much Lower Inside Park than Surrounding Highways
data.description: Speed limits for the park include 30 MPH near the park boundary and Great Sand Dunes Sign, and as low as 10 MPH near the Headquarters and Entrance Station. Speed limits are in place to protect park visitors, pedestrians, and wildlife in the park. Please drive carefully and responsibly.

data.title: Buildings located on the farm side are closed
data.description: Buildings located on the farm side of Hampton National Historic Site are closed due to construction related to the ongoing Legacy Restoration Fund Project. Visit the project webpage for more information or click the link to learn more.

data.title: Angels Landing Pilot Permit Program
data.description: Everyone who hikes Angels Landing needs to have a permit. Learn why you need a permit and how to get one. This requirement does not affect entering the park or riding the park shuttle (when it is running).

data.title: RV and trailer precautions: be aware of vehicle restrictions before visit.
data.description: As the busy season ramps up, traffic will be denser and can result in delays and complications particularly for owners of longer vehicles. The Tucson Mountain District (west side) of the park can accommodate vehicles up to 40ft in total length on the loop drive and has RV parking available at the Visitor Center, and the Rincon Mountain District (east side) can accommodate vehicles up to 40ft in length on the loop drive but has no RV parking available at the Visitor Center.

data.title: Application for Special Use Permit
data.description: Each applicant is required to complete a new "Application For Special Use Permit" prior to any new permit being issued

data.title: Vehicle Weight Limit at Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens Entrance
data.description: Due to structural conditions at the driveway entrance, access to the Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens main entrance and parking lot is limited to vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of 16,000 pounds or less.

data.title: Replace Bocce Ball Court Retaining Wall
data.description: Project work begins on Monday, February 9 to replace the bocce ball 50-foot retaining wall in order to improve existing infrastructure and enhance visitor safety. Several parking spots on lower Van Ness will be fenced off and the bocce ball court will not be accessible for the duration of the project, slated through August 2026. Please be aware of machinery, work, and signs.

data.title: Phone Lines Currently Down
data.description: The Whitman Mission NHS phone lines are currently down. If you need to contact us, please email whmi_interpretation. For field trip scheduling, please email whmi_education@nps.gov

data.title: Life Jackets Required!
data.description: By Nebraska State law, all children 13 years old and younger must WEAR a USCG approved life jacket to float the Niobrara NSR. Anyone over 13 years old must HAVE a life jacket. If you are renting equipment, your outfitter will provide them.

data.title: Staff Unable to Check Phone Messages at the Visitor Center
data.description: At this time, staff are unable to check or receive phone messages left at the visitor center. All calls to the park are being routed to Tuzigoot National Monument. You can also reach the park at moca_tuzi_info@nps.gov if you need to contact the park.

data.title: Dunes Drive Safety Corridor
data.description: Dunes Drive is open. A safety corridor is in effect between mile marker 3 and 5.5 along Dunes Drive. Visitors may drive but not stop or exit their vehicle in this area.

data.title: Temporary Phone Number for Visitor Center
data.description: Our main phone number for the visitor center is temporarily disconnected. Please call 307-877-4456 to reach a ranger.

data.title: Voicemail not functioning
data.description: The voicemail for the main park phone line (970-562-4282) is not functioning reliably. People are advised to call during business hours in order to speak with a ranger.

data.title: We Do Not Mail Junior Ranger Books
data.description: We do not mail Junior Ranger books; please download from site. Completed books may be submitted digitally. Junior Ranger badges may be mailed once per person per calendar year after completion. We do not mail completed books back.

data.title: Hospital wing, dining hall, shower room closed for rehabilitation work
data.description: Until approximately 2028, a portion of the cell house will be closed to visitors for important historic preservation work. We apologize for any inconvenience. Learn more at https://www.nps.gov/alca/alcatraz-historic-preservation-projects.htm

data.title: Expect Long Waits at the Summit Entrance Station Before Sunset
data.description: Due to a high volume of traffic, cars may be temporarily turned around at the gate when capacity is reached. Purchasing a pass online does not guarantee entry at sunset. To ensure timely access, arrive 3 hours before sunset.

data.title: David Wills House Closure
data.description: The David Wills House is currently closed. No known reopening date is available. Please visit our David Wills House web page for more information and a 3D tour of the house.

data.title: Limited Parking and Traffic Delays in Summit District
data.description: Beginning Monday, January 12, 2026 Haleakalā Visitor Center (summit district) parking lot will have limited parking due to a water infrastructure project. Expect traffic delays. The project will last several months.

data.title: Equestrian Traffic Temporarily Prohibited - Mile 124.5 to 155
data.description: Horses are prohibited between Little Tonoloway (mile 124.5) and Paw Paw (mile 155) due to recent and ongoing towpath resurfacing. See more for details.

data.title: Pet Policy
data.description: Pets are not allowed inside the visitor center at Aztec Ruins or on the trail through the Aztec West Great House. Pets are welcome in the parking lot, the picnic area, and along the Old Spanish Trail. Service animals are the only exception. Emotional support, therapy, and companion animals are not considered service animals and therefore not permitted in the visitor center or on the trail through Aztec West.

data.title: Museum to Remain Open During Construction
data.description: The Oklahoma City National Memorial Museum, Outdoor Symbolic Memorial, and Book Store will remain open during the construction of Foreward - a new Chapter of the museum. Visitors will enter through a new entrance on the southwest corner of the building. A temporary Visitor Experience Center has been placed near the museum for visitors to purchase tickets and browse Memorial merchandise. For more information on Foreward, please visit http://www.memorialmuseum.com.

data.title: Water is Required
data.description: Due to the trail being steep of 12 percent grade, all visitors wishing to hike the Lower Cliff Dwelling Trail must bring a water bottle with them. No Exceptions.

data.title: The Use of Drones is Prohibited at Big South Fork National River & Recreation Area
data.description: Currently, the use of drones is prohibited at Big South Fork and all National Parks. Detailed information about the policy is available...

data.title: Staple Bend Tunnel Closure
data.description: Due to a rockfall, the interior of the Staple Bend Tunnel is closed. The trail is still open. From the Mineral Point Trailhead, visitors can bypass the tunnel, via a path around the right side of the tunnel structure.

data.title: Ride Share Services - pickup limited
data.description: Taxi and ride-share services are often not available in Pecos. Even if services like Uber and Lyft will bring you here, it can be very difficult to secure a ride out. Please ensure you have a departure plan in place before being dropped off at Pecos.

data.title: Sand Board and Sand Sled Rentals Not Available In Park.
data.description: Sand boarding and sand sled rentals are located in local communities surrounding the park. Visitors are encouraged to arrange rentals BEFORE coming to the park.

data.title: Parking Reservations Always Required
data.description: Reservations are required for all personal vehicles and shuttle riders visiting Muir Woods. You can make your reservation by visiting www.gomuirwoods.com. Visit our "Know Before You Go" webpage to learn more important details before your visit.

data.title: No Cell Service at Muir Woods
data.description: There is NO cell service at Muir Woods. We discourage scheduling a rideshare service to leave the park. When hiring a taxi, visitors have the option of negotiating a flat rate or using the meter. Under some circumstances a flat rate may be cheaper.

data.title: Park Wide Caution
data.description: Visitors should exercise caution when hiking areas of the park. Hazards on trails and in forested areas such as hanging tree limbs, debris on the ground, and washed-out sections of trails and bridges are possible.

data.title: Park Wide Caution
data.description: Visitors should exercise caution when hiking areas of the park that have opened since Hurricane Helene. Hazards on trails and in forested areas such as hanging tree limbs, debris on the ground, and washed-out sections of trails and bridges are possible.

data.title: Phone Lines Down
data.description: Our phone lines are being upgraded and are currently down. If you need to contact us please email: NISI_Information@nps.gov Or you may call Cowpens National Battlefield at: 864 461-2828

data.title: We cannot mail out at this time
data.description: We do not mail Junior Ranger books; please download from site. Completed books may be submitted digitally. Junior Ranger badges may be mailed once per person per calendar year after completion. We do not mail completed books back.
